Created by combining {{D|Heat}} and {{D|Toxin}} damage. {{D|Gas}} produces gas clouds that deal damage to all enemies within a 3 meter radius for a short duration.|In-game Description}} {{D|Gas}} '''Damage''' is one of the six secondary elemental damage types, composed of {{D|Heat}} and {{D|Toxin}} elements. Deals increased damage to {{D|Infested Deimos}} and {{D|Techrot}} enemies but reduced damage against {{D|Scaldra}} enemies. Its [[Status Effect]] creates a damaging cloud that deals {{D|Gas}} [[Damage over Time]]. ==[[Status Effect]]s== ===General=== The status effect of {{D|Gas}} damage is '''Gas Cloud'''. It produces a gas cloud that deals a tick of damage each second to all enemies within a '''3'''-meter radius; subsequent procs increase the radius by '''0.3''' meters up to '''6 '''meters in total after '''10''' stacks. The cloud has a '''6''' second duration. Each tick deals {{D|Gas}} damage equal to: : { \begin{aligned} \text{Gas Proc Damage per Tick} &= 0.5 \times \text{Modded Base Damage} \\ &\qquad \times (1 + \text{Gas Damage Bonuses}) \\ &\qquad \times (1 + \text{Faction Damage Bonuses}) \\ &\qquad \times (1 + \text{Status Damage Bonuses}) \\ &\qquad \times \text{Additional Multipliers} \end{aligned} } ::''Gas Damage Bonuses include {{M|Valence Formation}}.'' ::''Additional Multipliers include modded critical multiplier on [[Critical Hit]] and multipliers on [[Enemy Body Parts]]; these stack multiplicatively with each other.'' :Modded Base Damage is not the same as normal damage calculations, ignoring physical and elemental damage bonuses and calculated as: :: { \begin{aligned} \text{Modded Base Damage} &= \text{Base Damage} \times (1 + \text{Base Damage Bonuses}) \times (1 + \text{Faction Damage Bonuses}) \end{aligned} } As can be seen from the formula, tick damage scales with {{D|Gas}} mods ({{D|Heat}} and {{D|Toxin}} mods have no effect). Up to '''10''' instances of the effect can stack on the same target, with each instance having its own timer. Any instances after the 10th will replace the oldest instance. The Gas Cloud is able to hit heads and other [[Enemy Body Parts|body parts]] by itself. However, the Gas Cloud itself has a '''1x''' damage bonus when headshotting. This can be increased with the use of mods such as {{M|Target Acquired}}, zoom bonuses on some [[Sniper Rifle|sniper rifles]], or {{Arcane|Primary Deadhead}}/{{Arcane|Secondary Deadhead}}. Example 1 ({{D|Heat}} and {{D|Toxin}} mods), tick damage for a weapon with an innate 180 damage, {{M|Hornet Strike}}, {{M|Scorch}}, {{M|Pathogen Rounds}}, {{M|Expel Grineer}}, and {{M|Pistol Elementalist}} will be: :Modded Base Damage = {{Math|180 {{mul}} (1 + 2.2) {{mul}} (1 + 0.3)|t=y|bf-a=y}} :'''Tick Damage''' = {{Math|0.5 {{mul}} 748.8 {{mul}} (1 + 0.3) {{mul}} (1 + 0.9)|t=y|bf-a=y}} Example 2 ({{D|Gas}} mod), tick damage for the {{Weapon|Vesper 77}} with {{M|Hornet Strike}}, {{M|Leaded Gas}}, {{M|Expel Grineer}}, and {{M|Pistol Elementalist}} will be: :Modded Base Damage = {{Math|180 {{mul}} (1 + 2.2) {{mul}} (1 + 0.3)|t=y|bf-a=y}} :'''Tick Damage''' = {{Math|0.5 {{mul}} 748.8 {{mul}} (1 + 3) {{mul}} (1 + 0.3) {{mul}} (1 + 0.9)|t=y|bf-a=y}} As can be seen in the above calculations for tick damage, Faction Damage is applied twice, making their effective bonus {{MathText|{{eql}} (1 + Faction Damage bonus)2}}. Which is +69% for the 30% Faction Damage mods and +140.25% for the 55% Primed Faction Damage mods. If the host target dies, {{D|Gas}} will continue to tick damage on all enemies caught in the host's radius for its remaining duration. A {{D|Gas}} proc briefly creates a dark green cloud on the afflicted. {| class="wikitable" |+ Gas tick damage and proc duration |- ! Collected Health Orbs add '''10s / 15s / 20s'''. ==Bugs== *{{D|Gas Cloud}} is misaligned on all units with a {{E|Heavy Gunner}}-type body, both the procs applied through a headshot and the lingering clouds from dead enemies often miss the head. ==Trivia== *Gas damage, with its brown color, damage over time, and its extra lethality to Deimos {{Faction|Infested}}, is likely a reference or callback to [https://darksector.fandom.com/wiki/Enferon Enferon], a gas that is highly lethal to creatures infected by the [https://darksector.fandom.com/wiki/Technocyte_Virus Technocyte Virus] but not uninfected humans in Digital Extremes' earlier title, [[wikipedia:Dark_Sector|Dark Sector]]. **This is further expanded with the weakness {{Faction|Techrot}} possess, as well as the existence of [[Efervon Sample|Efervon]], a very similarly named substance used by {{Faction|Scaldra}} against the Techrot. Scaldra are also resistant to Gas damage. ==Media== Screenshot_515.png|Gas visuals on a melee weapon Screenshot_516.png|Gas procs on an enemy ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|38.5}} *Fixed Gas Status Effect VFX not showing up. {{ver|37}} *Fixed Gas damage’s radial damage bubble VFX disappearing after hitting 10 stacks on the target. **It should now only disappear after all Gas stacks have expired. {{ver|36}} ;Simplified Faction Resistances *Deimos Infested: **Vulnerable to '''Gas''' ;Status Effect Reworks '''Gas''' Gas often lacked effective readability, making it difficult to distinguish its presence from the enemy or yourself. We’ve introduced enhanced visuals so that when the Gas Status Effect is active, you’ll be able to recognize it more clearly. '''Gas Changes:''' *Added VFX on top of the target affected by a Gas Cloud to clearly show an effect is active. **In addition to current and new VFX, Gas VFX now also more clearly shows the radius of the Gas Damage-over-Time (DoT) effect around a given target to better understand its impact on surrounding enemies. ***If a player is inside the radius of the Gas DoT, the visuals are reduced for them to maintain visibility, similar to Frost’s Snow Globe. *Gas VFX now has billowy volume to better present presence. *Gas VFX now has additional floating particles around the smoke. {{ver|33.5}} *Fixed a rare crash that could occur when using Enemy Radar and weapons that create Gas Status Effects. {{ver|27.3}} *Gas Effects will continue to tick radial Damage-over-Time for the average of the remaining Effect duration if their host dies. *Gas Status Area-of-Effect radius increases with the number of stacks, to a max of 10 stacks. *Removed Gas damage resistance from Toxic Ancient Auras. {{ver|27.2}} *The base duration of a Gas Status Effect now matches Slash for 6 seconds. No longer does AoE with forced Poison Status Effect (resulting in Poison DoT for enemies in radius), instead it does AoE DoT Gas damage around the target. {{ver|11}} *Introduced. }} ==See Also== *[[Truth]] {{DamageNav}} [[es:Daño Gas]] [[fr:Dégâts/Dégâts_Gaz]] [[ru:Урон/Газ]] {{DISPLAYTITLE:Gas Damage}} [[Category:Gas Damage]] [[Category:Damage 3.0]] [[Category:Damage]] [[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Update 11]]

Created by combining {{D|Cold}} and {{D|Electricity}} damage. {{D|Magnetic}} increases Shield and Overguard damage by up to 325% with multiple stacks and disables the target's Shield regeneration for a short duration. When Shield or Overguard breaks, deal Electricity Damage for 3% of enemy's Max Shield or Overguard per stack with a forced {{D|Electricity}} Status Effect.|In-game Description}} '''{{D|Magnetic}} Damage''' is one of the six secondary elemental damage types, composed of {{D|Cold}} and {{D|Electricity}} elements. Deals increased damage to {{D|Corpus}}, {{D|Corpus Amalgam}}, and {{D|Techrot}} enemies, but reduced damage against {{D|Narmer}} enemies. It is particularly effective at destroying [[Nullifier Crewman|nullifier bubbles]], and its [[Status Effect]] increases damage dealt to [[Shield]]s and {{D|Overguard}}, negates shield regeneration, and inflicts an {{D|Electricity}} proc upon removing all defenses. ==[[Status Effect]]s== ===General=== {{for|the game mode|Disruption}} The status effect of {{D|Magnetic}} damage is '''Disrupt'''. It amplifies damage to the [[Shield]]s and {{D|Overguard}} of the afflicted target by '''100%''' and reduces natural shield regeneration for '''6''' seconds. Subsequent procs add '''25%''' increased damage to Shields/Overguard up to '''325%''' in total after '''10''' stacks, with each stack having their own duration. Any stacks applied after the 10th will replace the oldest stack. { \begin{aligned} \text{Resultant Damage to Shields} &= \text{Modded Damage} \times [2 + (0.25 \times (\text{Number of Magnetic Stacks} - 1) ) ] \end{aligned} } ::''Calculating resultant damage if at least one Magnetic proc is on target. [[Damage Vulnerability]] provided by Magnetic procs are multiplicative with other damage bonuses.'' Upon breaking of the Shields/Overguard the target receives a forced {{D|Electricity}} proc that deals a total of '''3%''' of the target's maximum Shields/Overguard per {{D|Magnetic}} status effect, to a maximum of '''30%''' at full stacks, over a period of '''6 seconds'''. The damage of the forced {{D|Electricity}} proc is determined by the weapon or ability that applied the magnetic status. *Base damage mods like {{M|Serration}} mods have '''no''' effect. *Status damage mods like {{M|Pistol Elementalist}} are applied '''twice''', multiplying the damage by '''3.61''' *Faction damage modifiers like {{M|Expel Corpus}} are applied twice. *Electric damage mods like {{M|Convulsion}} are applied like normal even if they are combined into another status effect. *Status duration mods are applied like normal and are a final multiplier to the total damage. *[[Archon Stretch]] Will apply when the forced [[electricity]] proc from breaking [[Overguard]] is applied but only from abilities that can apply [[Magnetic status]] Effects that restore shields, such as {{E|Shield Osprey|Shield Osprey's}} and {{E|Orokin Drone|Orokin Drone's}} shield links, will bypass {{D|Magnetic}}'s recharge penalty. Affected [[Tenno]] suffer additional effects: their [[HUD]]s will be distorted and have '''30''' {{D|Energy Drain}} damage dealt to them per second for '''3''' seconds; The first tick is dealt instantly, resulting in '''4''' ticks in total. {{D|Energy Drain}} is dealt directly to the players energy bar, resulting in a loss of '''30''' [[energy]] per tick, for a total energy loss of '''120''' energy over the duration of the status effect. Status cleanse will stop the energy drain and the HUD static. {{D|Magnetic}} procs will show blue rings matching the shape of the affected target moving from top to bottom. ===Railjack=== {{D|Magnetic}} does not have a [[Railjack]] space counterpart and is thus not able to proc any status effect nor is it included in calculations for status proc weighting. ==Magnetic Sources== {{Main|:Category:Magnetic Damage}} ===Weapons=== {{Main|:Category:Magnetic Damage Weapons}} {{DamageTypeTable|Magnetic}} Opticor.png|link=Opticor|{{Weapon|Opticor}} (Explosion)|alt=Opticor (Explosion) OpticorVandal.png|link=Opticor Vandal|{{Weapon|Opticor Vandal}} (Explosion)|alt=Opticor Vandal (Explosion) Halikar.png|link=Halikar|{{Weapon|Halikar}} (Slam Attack)|alt=Halikar (Slam Attack) Kogake.png|link=Kogake|{{Weapon|Kogake}} ([[Kogake Prime|Prime]]) (Wall Attack)|alt=Kogake (Prime) (Wall Attack) Kestrel.png|link=Kestrel|{{Weapon|Kestrel}} ([[Kestrel Prime|Prime]]) (Slam Attack)|alt=Kestrel (Slam Attack) Do also note that [[Adversary#Adversary Weapons|adversary weapons]] such as the {{Weapon|Kuva Nukor}} may come with a Magnetic damage benefit of up to 60% as long as the progenitor matches. MeleeVortex.png|link=Melee Vortex|{{Arcane|Melee Vortex}}|alt=Melee Vortex PrimaryObstruct.png|link=Primary Obstruct|{{Arcane|Primary Obstruct}}|alt=Primary Obstruct == Trivia == Being a combination of {{D|Cold}} and{{D|Electricity}}, it's likely that {{D|Magnetic}} is derived from [[w:Superconductivity|superconductors]], materials that conduct electricity with high efficiency at low temperature. ==Media== Screenshot_518.png|Magnetic proc on an enemy Screenshot_517.png|Magnetic visuals on a melee weapon, with effects similar to those of cold and electric {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|AaE6VXtxMRw|size=300px}} }} == Bugs == ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|38.5}} *Updated tooltip for Magnetic Status to communicate the bonus damage against Overguard. {{ver|36}} ;Simplified Faction Resistances *Corpus: Vulnerable to '''Magnetic''' *Narmer: **Resistant to '''Magnetic''' *Corpus Amalgam: **Resistant to '''Magnetic''' ;Status Effect Reworks '''Magnetic''' Magnetic has received a few buffs to increase its effectiveness against Shields and to hammer home the power fantasy of overloading enemy Shields. '''Magnetic Changes:''' *Damage to Nullifier Bubbles has been increased **Minimum Damage raised to 300 Damage per shot. **Maximum Damage raised to 1200 Damage per shot. ***Additionally, we now show the minimum and maximum damage numbers against Nullifier Bubbles, with Magnetic attacks displaying the buffed damage shown above, while non-Magnetic sources will display the original, unbuffed damage. ****Known issue: Clients see the incorrectly unbuffed damage from Magnetic sources, which is strictly a UI/visual bug. Magnetic sources will continue to deal increased damage towards Nullifier Bubbles despite the incorrect numbers displayed. We will look to resolve this in a future Hotfix/Update. *Reduced Shield Regeneration by a percentage per Magnetic stack against affected targets. *Upon Shield/Overguard Breaking a target, the enemy will now be dealt Electric Status damage for a percentage of Max Shields/Overguard per Magnetic stack while also forcing an Electric Status Effect. *Magnetic stacks on an enemy with Overguard now allow for bonus damage to Overguard, similar to how Magnetic affects Shields. {{ver|35}} *Reduced the duration of Magnetic Status Effects when applied to players from 6 to 3 seconds and decreased the total Energy drain from 120 to 90. **In addition to general feedback on Magnetic Damage being a bit harsh, the new tileset has many Magnetic Damage sources so the following changes were made to ensure it still had an impact without becoming unmanageable. {{ver|31.6}} *Reduced the Energy drain from Magnetic procs from 50 to 20 per tick. **This not only applies to Thrax enemies, but to Magnetic damage across the game (laser doors, magnetic water in the Plains of Eidolon, etc.)! A default Magnetic proc used to drain 250 Energy, now it will do 100. {{ver|27.2}} *New Status Effect entirely: enhanced Damage! First Magnetic Status Effect deals 100% additional Shield damage, subsequent Magnetic Status add +25% for a total of 325% (capped). Enemies under a Magnetic Status Effect cannot regenerate Shields. Magnetic Status Duration is now 6 seconds. {{ver|22}} *Magnetic Damage Status Effects now drain energy over time as opposed to completely draining all energy. {{ver|19}} * Fixed an issue where a Magnetic Status Effect would typically lower the victim's Shields further upon expiry (rather than restore them properly) if it had re-triggered the Status Effect. {{ver|11}} *Introduced. }} ==See Also== *[[Entropy]] {{DamageNav}} [[es:Daño Magnético]] [[fr:Dégâts/Dégâts Magnétique]] [[ru:Урон/Магнит]] {{DISPLAYTITLE:Magnetic Damage}} [[Category:Magnetic Damage]] [[Category:Damage 3.0]] [[Category:Damage]] [[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Update 11]] [[Category:Damage Vulnerability]]

{{Top|Lotus|Tenno|Tenno|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Daikyu takes great strength to draw back, but provides added power and range to every shot.}} The '''Daikyu''' is an asymmetrical bow of {{Faction|Tenno}} design and origin. It has larger damage, [[status chance]] and increased [[Projectile Speed]] compared to the other bows, as well as high [[critical chance]], but takes longer to fully draw and cannot be released early for decreased damage. ==Characteristics== *This weapon primarily deals {{D|Puncture}} damage. *Guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc. **Can fully benefit of {{M|Internal Bleeding}}. *Charged shots have an innate 3 meter [[punch through]], the highest of all bows. **As it can only be fired when fully charged, shots will always have the [[punch through]]. *On kill, bodies will follow the arrow that killed them, damaging anyone in their path and pinning the corpse to walls. *Medium-to-high [[zoom]] level when aiming. *Can equip the bow-exclusive {{M|Thunderbolt}} mod, and the Daikyu-exclusive {{M|Spring-Loaded Broadhead}} and {{M|Amalgam Daikyu Target Acquired}} mods. *[[Fire rate]] mods apply double their bonuses. *Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} polarity. {{Advantages|class=Bow| *Highest shot base damage of all bows. (without counting the AOE effect of {{Weapon|Proboscis Cernos}},{{Weapon|Kuva Bramma}}, and {{Weapon|Lenz}}) *Second highest [[status chance]] of all bows, behind {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}. *Second fastest [[Projectile Speed]] of all primary weapons, behind {{Weapon|Lanka}}. *Fastest [[Projectile Speed]] of all bows. **Arrows have low arc due to flight speed. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Bow| *Second slowest [[Fire Rate|charge speed]] of all bows, after {{Weapon|Lenz}}. **Cannot be fired at partial charge. *Arrows have travel time with slight arcing. }} {{WeaponComparison|Daikyu Prime}} ==Acquisition== The Daikyu's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Tenno Lab|Tenno Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Notes== *The Daikyu does not have a quick fire option, nor can it be fired at partial charge - it must be fully charged before it can be fired. **The weapon's charge, both in its draw phase and its hold phase, can be cancelled by performing actions that will break normal weapon charges, such as pressing reload, rolling, or switching to another weapon. *The Daikyu reportedly does not benefit from multiplicative gun CO from Galvanized Aptitude. Instead, it acts the same as damage mods like Serration, Heavy Caliber, or gun Arcanes like Primary Merciless. ==Tips== *This weapon is perfect for {{M|Internal Bleeding}}: with the guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc and slow fire rate, each arrow has 70% chance to apply bleed. **With {{M|Internal Bleeding}} + {{M|Vile Acceleration}} + {{M|Critical Delay}}, the weapon has guaranteed crit (120%), a fast charge time (0.42s), and is still just above the threshold to have 70% proc rate from Internal Bleeding. * The increased [[Projectile Speed]] and subsequent low arc makes it much easier to achieve headshots and hit enemies at very long ranges. * {{M|Speed Trigger}}, ({{M|Primed Shred|Primed}}) {{M|Shred}}, {{M|Vigilante Fervor}} and {{M|Vile Acceleration}} can be used individually or in combination to speed up the Daikyu's draw speed. ==Trivia== *The ''daikyū'' (大弓) is one of two variants of the Japanese asymmetrical ''[[wikipedia:Yumi|yumi]]'' bow. Read as "big bow" or "Longbow", the ''daikyū'' is the larger variant to the smaller ''hankyū'' (半弓; lit. "half bow"). *The mechanics of this bow appear to be heavily based on the principles of ''[[wikipedia:Kyūdō|Kyūdō]]'', the practice of Japanese archery. By taking one's time and adopting proper shooting posture and form, the arrow is assured to hit its mark. *The Codex description mentions great strength required to draw the Daikyu, which may refer to its prolonged drawing time. *The Daikyu was the first bow that has a completely compact, collapsible form when holstered. It folds into three pieces: its two arms and the grip, creating a U-shape as the arms point upward on the player's back. The {{Weapon|Lenz}} would follow as the second, folding in a similar manner. ==Media== Update16_5_Day3Weapons-AsymmetricalBow.jpg|Preview image of the Daikyu. Daikyu Arsenal.png|Daikyu in Arsenal Daikyu Arsenal 2.png Daikyu Arsenal 3.png Daikyu when Holstered.png|Daikyu when Holstered {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|Uub7Mjer8nk|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|43.5.4}} *Fixed Daiku and Daiku Prime's animations being broken with certain bow skins equipped. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. {{Navigation|Damage|Damage/Calculation|Damage/Overview Table}} {{Successor |precededby=Damage 2.0 |precededbysince={{ver|36}} }} {{Infobox | Box title = Damage | image = DamageModBundleIcon.png }} '''Damage''' (version 3.0) is a system that determines the damage done to a certain target by a given attacker. Damage results are modified by several mechanics – [[Damage Type Modifier|damage type modifiers]] (main content of this article), [[armor]], [[Critical Hit|critical hit bonuses]], [[stealth|stealth bonuses]], [[Warframes|Warframe ability debuffs]], [[Enemy Body Parts|body part modifiers]], [[Faction Damage Mods|faction modifiers]], and other sources of [[Damage Reduction|damage reduction]] – which are discussed below and on their respective pages. All damage dealt by any weapon or ability belongs to a certain damage type, and every target has specific resistances and vulnerabilities to different damage types. In-game, enemy resistances and vulnerabilities can be seen in the player's [[Codex]] after scanning at least one enemy of a particular type or by aiming at an enemy using the [[Synthesis Scanner]] with the ''Data-Parse Widget''. Exploiting enemy vulnerabilities and avoiding resistances by means of weapon selection and mod installation may significantly improve players' damage output. Since its predecessor [[Damage 2.0]], all different Health, Armor, and Shield types have been simplified into one type for each (e.g. Grineer's {{D|Cloned Flesh}} and {{D|Machinery}} is now just "Health", {{D|Ferrite Armor}} and {{D|Alloy Armor}} is now just "Armor", and {{D|Shield}} and {{D|Proto Shield}} is now just "Shield"). Vulnerabilities and resistances have also been decoupled from health types and are now solely based on the enemy [[Faction]] (e.g. all {{D|Grineer}} are now exclusively vulnerable to {{D|Impact}} and {{D|Corrosive}} at all times, regardless of the presence of armor or shields, and no longer have any resistances). ==Damage Display== {{Main|Damage Numbers}} [[File:Crit_numbers.png|thumb|Three different color tiers of critical hits along with normal damage color]] Damage dealt from players to enemies is displayed on the [[HUD]] as numbers near the point of impact on an enemy. Damage dealt from enemies to players is displayed on the HUD both as a bent strip to indicate its direction of origin and as a reduction in shield or health [[Hit Points]] to indicate its quantity. Each individual projectile or melee attack will display a single damage instance whose value is rounded to the nearest integer. Weapons with multiple projectiles like shotguns or rifles with [[Multishot]] will display a damage instance for each individual projectile. Weapons that fire continuously will display a damage instance at a constant rate depending on the fire rate of the weapon. Damage indicators are color-coded using the following system (default UI colors): * Damage appears by default in white (◼). * [[Ability]] damage appears by default in purple (◼). * [[Critical Hit|Critical hits]], also called 'Base Critical Hits', and [[stealth|stealth attacks]] are in yellow (◼). * [[Critical Hit#Critical Levels|Orange crits]], also called 'Big Critical Hits', appear in orange (◼). These are stronger than yellow crits. * [[Critical Hit#Critical Levels|Red crits]], also called 'Super Critical Hits', as their name suggests, appear in red (◼). These are stronger than orange crits. * Damage against [[shields]] and [[overshields]] appears in blue (◼), regardless of other factors such as critical hits. * Attempts to damage an invulnerable enemy appear in grey (◼). ==Overview Table== {{Transclude|Damage/Overview Table}} ==Damage Types== Every weapon, ability or method of dealing damage is classified as one or more types of damage. Through mods or abilities, further types of damage can be added to attacks. When multiple damage types are present on an attack, all of them will deal their respective amounts independent of each other, but only one damage number calculated from the combined value of the damage types will show. With each shown damage value, there is also a chance of a [[Status Effect]] occurring; the likelihood of which type of damage this Status Effect is based on depends on the percent distribution of the damage types on the weapon. ===Physical Damage=== Most weapons' base damage is made up of a combination of three physical damage types: {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Puncture}}, and {{D|Slash}}. On Player: Reduces armor by '''26%''' for '''8''' seconds. |- |} ====Modding==== '''Elemental Damage Combinations''' are made by following a mod placement hierarchy. This hierarchy is from closest to top left (first to be considered) to the bottom right (last to be considered) on the mod layout. Innate weapon elemental damages are considered the very last in any hierarchy, with one exception: some Kuva and Tenet weapons from [[Kuva Lich]]es or [[Sisters of Parvos]] are capable of having two base elemental damages (one from the weapon, one from the Valence damage of the Progenitor Warframe that made the Lich/Sister). In these cases, whichever of the two primary elements comes first in this element order - {{D|Heat}} > {{D|Cold}} > {{D|Electricity}} > {{D|Toxin}}, or '''"HCET"''' for short - will be placed second to last in the element combine order, while the other primary element will be placed last in the combine order. However, a weapon's innate elemental damage can be forced into a different position in the hierarchy (and thus be combined into a secondary element earlier) if the player has equipped a mod of the same element as the innate element. As well, when using multiple mods with the same element, the first position that element is placed in establishes its hierarchy and where it's combined. For example, putting {{M|Stormbringer}} on the top left slot of an {{Weapon|Amprex}} will change the position of its innate {{D|Electricity}} damage from last in hierarchy to first in hierarchy. Similarly, placing {{M|Thermite Rounds}} earlier in the hierarchy before placing {{M|Hellfire}} will still count the {{D|Heat}} damage where it was first placed. A weapon's innate elemental damage will contribute to elemental combinations, as long as the combination has been established earlier in the hierarchy. It can also combine with the last uncombined elemental mod in the hierarchy to form a secondary element. [[File:LoadOrder.png|thumb|left|Load Order]] For example: when modding a weapon with {{D|Electricity}} such as the {{Weapon|Prova}} or the {{Weapon|Lecta}}, then adding {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Toxin}}, and {{D|Heat}} in 1, 2 and 3 respectively get: {{D|Viral}} ({{D|Cold}} + {{D|Toxin}}) and {{D|Radiation}} ({{D|Heat}} + {{D|Electricity}}). In the case of [[Riven Mods]] where there is more than one elemental stat present, the hierarchy priority will be given to the '''last''' elemental stat listed on the Riven mod. For example, a Riven mod with a bonus of +100% {{D|Electricity}} damage first and +90% {{D|Toxin}} damage last, will enable the {{D|Toxin}} damage to combine with an elemental mod higher up in the hierarchy, and the {{D|Electricity}} damage will combine with an elemental damage type lower in the hierarchy. If no other elemental damage mods are present, the elements on the Riven mod will combine with itself. Weapons with innate secondary elements such as {{Weapon|Ogris}} ({{D|Blast}}), {{Weapon|Penta}} ({{D|Blast}}), {{Weapon|Stug}} ({{D|Corrosive}}), {{Weapon|Nukor}} ({{D|Radiation}}) and {{Weapon|Detron}} ({{D|Radiation}}) will '''always''' have that damage type, regardless of mods used. On weapons like these, basic elemental damage mods will combine and function ''independently'' of the innate secondary elements, as basic elements '''cannot''' combine with a weapon's already combined innate damage type. [[Kuva Weapons]] and [[Tenet Weapons]] will follow this behavior too. For example, a {{Weapon|Tenet Detron}} ({{D|Radiation}}) can come with an additional {{D|Electricity}} Progenitor damage bonus that will '''not''' add onto the innate {{D|Radiation}} damage. '''Dealing damage is [[wikipedia:Quantization|quantized]].''' Meaning, rather than the damage being applied smoothly, physical and elemental damages round to the nearest multiple of 1/32nd of their attack's base damage, before being multiplied further.<ref>{{Ref|title=Internal rounding leading to unintended applied damage|author= Theroxenes|year=2018|month=3|day=2|publisher=Warframe Forums|url=https://forums.warframe.com/topic/928927-internal-rounding-leading-to-unintended-applied-damage/|access-date=2022-09-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220919171910/https://forums.warframe.com/topic/928927-internal-rounding-leading-to-unintended-applied-damage/|archive-date=2022-09-19}}</ref><ref>{{Ref|title=Internal damage quantization or: Another way the arsenal is lying to you.|author=Theroxenes|year=2018|month=2|day=28|publisher=Reddit|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/Warframe/comments/809yaa/internal_damage_quantization_or_another_way_the/|access-date=2022-09-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211124174002/https://www.reddit.com/r/Warframe/comments/809yaa/internal_damage_quantization_or_another_way_the/|archive-date=2021-11-24}}</ref> By using this method of quantization, the precision of data is reduced, thereby saving storage space and improving the efficiency of computer operations. Rather than communicating a lengthy integer of each element's value, only one "Total" integer along with short representative multiples of 1/32nd need to be communicated.

<math>
{
\text{Scale} = \frac{\text{Modded Base Damage}}{32}
}
</math>

For each damage type, first express its value as a signed proportion of the modded base damage:

<math>
x = \frac{\text{Total Damage Type Value}}{\text{Modded Base Damage}}
</math>

The exact quantization rule is:

<math>
\operatorname{Quantized}(x)
= \operatorname{sign}(x) \times \frac{\left\lfloor |x| \times 32 + 0.5 \right\rfloor}{32}
</math>

The quantized damage type value is then:

<math>
\text{Quantized Damage Type Value}
= \operatorname{Quantized}(x) \times \text{Modded Base Damage}
</math>

For non-negative values, this is equivalent to dividing the damage type value by the scale, applying <math>\left\lfloor y+0.5\right\rfloor</math>, and multiplying by the scale. For negative values, the same operation is applied to the absolute magnitude before restoring the sign. This quantized value is used in mission damage calculations. The final damage seen in damage pop-ups is further rounded to a whole number.

# For example, if you have a weapon with a listed damage distribution of 30 {{D|Impact}}, 30 {{D|Puncture}}, and 40 {{D|Slash}}, the total damage is '''100'''.
# The value of a scale will then be {{Math|100 {{div}} 32|t=y|bf-a=y}}.
# The amount of {{D|Impact}} damage dealt by the weapon will then be {{Math|30 {{div}} 3.125|t=y}} rounded to the nearest whole number, multiplied by the scale: {{Math|10 {{mul}} 3.125|t=y|bf-a=y}}.  This process is applied to {{D|Puncture}} and {{D|Slash}} as well, yielding '''31.25''' and '''40.625''' respectively.
# As such, when damaging a {{E|Charger}}, which has a +50% bonus to {{D|Slash}} damage due to having {{D|Infested}} health, the total damage dealt to the Charger will then be {{Math|31.25 + 31.25 + 40.625 {{mul}} (1 + 50%)|t=y|bf-a=y}} (the game will display the rounded value of {{Math|31.25 + 31.25 + 40.625 {{mul}} (1 + 50%)|round=1}}). 

*Note that while sometimes the weapon's total damage after the conversion remains the same, mixed-type weapon damage is frequently '''gained''' or '''lost''' by the conversion.

====Summary====
Calculating damage with quantization can be simplified to the following steps:
#Get Scale
#Quantize Physical and Elemental Damage
#Add quantized values together
#Apply all other multipliers such as [[Damage Type Modifier]]

====Trivia====
* [[Hitscan]] weapons do not quantize against {{D|Object}} health such as [[Nullifier Bubble]]s and {{WF|Zephyr}} {{A|Tornado}}. [[Projectile]]s however will be quantized. This characteristic has been used to determine damage compositions not disclosed in-game, so they can be presented here in the wiki.
* [[Melee]] weapons with very low {{D|Impact}} damage relative to other damage types will not trigger {{M|Shattering Impact}} due to quantization of the {{D|Impact}} damage value to 0. {{Weapon|Galatine}} for example has 2.5% {{D|Impact}} damage.
* Here is a comparison of space savings for using non-quantized vs. quantized values. As more damage types are present on the attack, the greater the space saving:
** If we use 64-bit floating-point values for each damage type (e.g. {{D|Impact}} = 30, {{D|Puncture}} = 30, {{D|Slash}} = 40), that's 3 × 64 bits = 192 bits
** If we use one 64-bit floating-point value for the total damage and a smaller 16-bit floating-point value for each damage type's scale (e.g. Total = 100, {{D|Impact}} = 9.6, {{D|Puncture}} = 9.6, {{D|Slash}} = 12.8), that's 64 bits + (3 × 16 bits) = 112 bits. Almost a 42% size reduction with the tradeoff of clients needing to recompute the damage and losing some precision!

===Unarmored Enemies===
Against '''unarmored''' enemies or when applying {{D|True}} damage, the formula is simply:

<math>
{
\text{Inflicted Damage} = \text{Starting Damage} (1 + \text{Health-type Modifier})
}
</math>

*'''Inflicted Damage (ID)''' is the final damage result of a particular damage type.
*'''Starting Damage (SD)''' is the initial damage value of a particular damage type, modded or not.
*'''Health-type Modifier (HM)''' is the damage modifier against that health type (may be shields or health).

<hr />
To make it independent from the amount of base damage:

<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Damage Modifier} &= 1 + \text{Health-type Modifier} \\
\text{Inflicted Damage} &= \text{Starting Damage} \times \text{Damage Modifier}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>

* '''Damage Modifier (DM)''' is the total damage modifier. An amount of damage of that type (SD) against that enemy will then always be multiplied with this factor (DM).

===Armored Enemies===
Against '''[[armor]]ed''' enemies, the formula is:

<math>
{
DM = 1 - 0.9 \cdot \sqrt\frac{{AR}}{2700}
}
</math>

Where in addition to the previous definitions, '''AR''' is the target's armor after all reductions from debuffs (e.g. {{M|Corrosive Projection}}, {{D|Corrosive}} status effects, and {{A|Terrify}}).

In the case of enemies who have both [[shields]] and armor, damage to shields is not mitigated by armor. Lastly, when {{D|Toxin}} damage is applied to a shielded target, generally the damage is applied directly to its health, not shields (i.e. it bypasses shields). Some special enemies like [[Treasurer]] or [[Hound]]s cannot have their shields bypassed with {{D|Toxin}} damage however.

===Total Damage===
The damage numbers displayed in the in-game [[arsenal]] calculate total weapon damage as such:

{| class="wikitable"
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Arsenal Total Damage} &= \text{Base Damage} \\
&\quad  \times [ 1 + \text{Elemental Bonuses} \\
&\qquad + \text{Unmodded Impact Distribution} \times \text{Impact Bonuses} \\
&\qquad + \text{Unmodded Puncture Distribution} \times \text{Puncture Bonuses} \\
&\qquad + \text{Unmodded Slash Distribution} \times \text{Slash Bonuses} ] \\
&\quad \times ( 1 + \text{Damage Bonuses}) \\
&\quad \times [\text{Base Weapon Multishot} \times ( 1 + \text{Multishot Bonuses})]
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
This arsenal damage is the average non-crit damage per shot, without [[Faction Damage Bonus]]. 
*For melee weapons, remove multishot from the equation. It does not include Stance damage multipliers.
|-
|}

Theoretical total inflicted damage against an enemy can be calculated as such (ignoring quantization for simplification):

{| class="wikitable"
|-
|
<math>
{
\text{Total Inflicted Damage} = \text{SD}_{1} \times \text{DM}_{1} + ... + \text{SD}_{N} \times \text{DM}_{N}
}
</math>
|
Where SD represents the modded value of a particular damage type and DM represents the damage modifier for a particular damage type using the generalized damage modifier formula.
|-
|}

===Average Shot/Hit===
Average shot or hit is the theoretical average damage dealt on a single button input if all projectiles hit the target.

{| class="wikitable"
|-
|
<math>
{
\text{Normal Shot} = \text{Total Damage} \times [1 + (\lfloor \text{Modded Crit Chance} \rfloor \times (\text{Modded Crit Multiplier} - 1) ) ]
}
</math>
|
In the case where modded critical chance is over 100%, the lowest crit tier possible will be considered a normal shot. (e.g. if a weapon has 250% crit chance, the 100% for an orange crit will be considered a normal shot)
*Note that <math>\lfloor \qquad \rfloor</math> denotes a [[wikipedia:Floor and ceiling_functions|flooring function]] (rounding down)
|-
|
<math>
{
\text{Critical Shot} = \text{Total Damage} \times [1 + (\lceil \text{Modded Crit Chance} \rceil \times (\text{Modded Crit Multiplier} - 1) ) ]
}
</math>
|
In the case where modded critical chance is over 100%, the next crit tier possible will be considered a critical shot (e.g. if a weapon has 250% crit chance, the 50% for a red crit will be considered a critical shot)
*Note that <math>\lceil \qquad \rceil</math> denotes a [[wikipedia:Floor and ceiling_functions|ceiling function]] (rounding up)
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average Shot} &= \text{Total Damage} \times (1 + \text{Modded Crit Chance} \times (\text{Modded Crit Multiplier} - 1))
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
The average damage dealt on a single button input if all projectiles hit the target.
|-
|}

===Gun Damage Per Second===
When comparing the performance of non-melee weapons, it may be useful to calculate their theoretical single-target damage per second (DPS) (without accounting for status effects) using the following formulas:

====Average Burst DPS====
Average burst DPS is the theoretical damage a player does in a very short burst of time, or an extended period of time if ignoring time spent reloading/not firing their weapon.

{| class="wikitable"
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average Burst DPS} &= \text{Average Shot} \times \text{Effective Fire Rate}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
Where effective fire rate calculations is dependent on trigger type. Arsenal Fire Rate stat ≠ actual rate of fire in-game
*Assumes that damage ramp up is at max for Continuous Weapons. In actual gameplay, reloading will reset/decay the damage ramp up so Burst DPS will be lower than theoretical calculations.
*Assumes fire rate is the arsenal value for Auto-Spooled trigger weapons.
|-
|}

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Effective Fire Rate formulas by Trigger Type
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Effective Fire Rate}_\text{Auto, Auto-Spool, Semi, Duplex, Held} &= \text{Modded Fire Rate}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
For Auto, Semi, Duplex, and Held trigger types, the modded Fire Rate is the effective Fire Rate.
*For Semi and Duplex trigger types, we assume the player is able to achieve the modded Fire Rate value via manual attack inputs.
*For Auto-Spool trigger types, we assume that the weapon is fully spooled to the arsenal Fire Rate value.
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Effective Fire Rate}_\text{Charge} &= \frac{ 1 }{ \text{Modded Charge Time} + \frac{ 1 }{ \text{Modded Fire Rate} } }
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
For Charge trigger types, the lower the [[Fire Rate]], the more delay between charge shots. If attack is not a Charge trigger type (Modded Charge Time = 0), then Effective Fire Rate = Modded Fire Rate. We assume the player immediately lets go for the attack key on full charge and doesn't delay the attack.
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Effective Fire Rate}_\text{Burst} = \frac{ \text{Burst Count} }{ \frac{1}{\text{Modded Fire Rate}} + [ (\text{Burst Count} - 1) \cdot \text{Burst Delay} ] }
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
For Burst trigger types, there is a delay between bursts (Fire Rate value) and a delay between shots in a burst (Burst Delay value). For Mag Burst attacks, use the full magazine size as the Burst Count. For non-Burst attacks, you can set Burst Count = 1 (can think of shooting a whole magazine as a single "burst" regardless of trigger type) which resolves to Effective Fire Rate = Modded Fire Rate.
|-
|}

====Number of Shots Per Magazine====
Actual magazine size is needed to calculate sustained DPS.

{| class="wikitable"
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of Shots Per Magazine} &= \frac{ \text{Modded Mag Size} }{ \text{Ammo Cost Per Shot} }
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
Not all weapons consume one ammo per shot; this formula is needed to account for [[Continuous Weapon]]s and certain alt-fires
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of Shots Per Magazine}_{Incarnon} &= \text{Max Incarnon Charge}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
For [[Incarnon Form]], use Max Incarnon Charge. Ammo Cost is 1 per shot
|-
|}

====Average Sustained DPS====
Average sustained DPS is the theoretical damage a player does over an extended period of time, accounting time spent reloading/not firing their weapon.

{| class="wikitable"
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Proportion of Time Spent Shooting vs. Reloading} &= \frac{ \text{Number of Shots Per Mag} }{ \text{Effective Fire Rate} \times \text{Modded Reload Time} + \text{Number of Shots Per Mag}}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
This ratio is a damage multiplier to multiply Burst DPS into Sustained DPS
*For the {{Weapon|Vectis}} and {{Weapon|Vectis Prime}} specifically, one (1) should be subtracted from the denominator to account for their lack of a [[reload]] delay.
*For {{Weapon|Epitaph}} specifically, ignore Modded Reload Time since it draws ammo directly from the full ammo pool similar to bows, but does not "reload" between shots like them.
*Reload time is in seconds.
*Reload time includes reload delay which is more prevalent for [[Battery Weapon]]s. Reload delay for most weapons are negligible if not non-existent.
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average Sustained DPS} &= \text{Average Burst DPS} \times \text{Proportion of Time Spent Shooting vs. Reloading}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
*Assumes that damage ramp up is at max for [[Continuous Weapon]]s. In actual gameplay, reloading will reset/decay the damage ramp up so Burst DPS will be lower than theoretical calculations.
|-
|}

Damage-over-time tick damage is not subject to the 1/32 damage-type [[#Quantization|quantization]] described above. A proc is calculated from the attack's modded base damage rather than from the sum of its quantized damage-type values. Critical DoTs use the effective critical multiplier of the inducing hit; exact calculations should apply the critical multiplier quantization described on [[Critical Hit]].

For exact calculations, intermediate DoT operations use [[wikipedia:Single-precision floating-point format|binary32]] arithmetic.

For weapon-generated {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Gas}}, and {{D|Slash}} status effects, the temporary damage accumulator for each tick group starts at 1 rather than 0. The full-precision damage seeds are then added to this accumulator before the status coefficient and the remaining applicable multipliers are applied:
:<math>\text{Unrounded Tick Damage} = \left(\sum_i S_i + 1\right) \times C \times M</math>
Here, <math>S_i</math> is each stored damage seed, <math>C</math> is 0.5 for Heat, Electricity, Toxin, and Gas or 0.35 for Slash, and <math>M</math> is the product of the remaining applicable modifiers, such as elemental, faction, and status-damage bonuses. If several seeds are consolidated into a single tick, they are added to the same accumulator, so its initial value of 1 is included only once. It is therefore neither a final flat +1 damage bonus nor a bonus applied once per status stack.

Examples, before target defenses:
* {{D|Heat}}: {{Weapon|Supra Vandal}} has <math>40</math> base damage. With {{M|Thermite Rounds}} (+60% Heat damage), <math>(40 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 1.6 = 32.8</math>, displayed as <math>33</math>.
* {{D|Electricity}} with a <math>40</math> seed and +150% Electricity damage: <math>(40 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 2.5 = 51.25</math>, displayed as <math>51</math>.
* {{D|Toxin}} with a <math>40</math> seed, +225% Toxin damage, and {{M|Primed Bane of Orokin}} (+55% faction damage): <math>(40 \times 1.55 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 3.25 \times 1.55 = 158.68</math>, displayed as <math>159</math>.
* {{D|Gas}} with a <math>40</math> seed and no applicable bonuses: <math>(40 + 1) \times 0.5 = 20.5</math>, displayed as <math>21</math>.
* {{D|Slash}} with a <math>40</math> seed and {{M|Primed Bane of Orokin}} (+55% faction damage): <math>(40 \times 1.55 + 1) \times 0.35 \times 1.55 = 34.18</math>, displayed as <math>34</math>.

* {{D|Gas}} with nine consolidated stacks—six critical seeds of <math>80.0195389</math> and three non-critical seeds of <math>40</math>: using binary32 operations, <math>(6 \times 80.0195389 + 3 \times 40 + 1) \times 0.5 = 300.558594</math>, displayed as <math>301</math>. The fixed value of 1 is added once after summing the seeds, not once per stack.
* {{D|Heat}} accumulates active stacks into one tick. With +60% Heat damage, one <math>40</math> seed and one <math>80.0195389</math> seed produce <math>(40 + 80.0195389 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 1.6 = 96.8156357</math>, displayed as <math>97</math>.
* {{D|Electricity}} proc instances keep their own durations, but contributions occurring on the same pulse are consolidated into one damage number. With +150% Electricity damage, the same two seeds produce <math>(40 + 80.0195389 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 2.5 = 151.274429</math>, displayed as <math>151</math>.
* {{D|Slash}} and {{D|Toxin}} stacks tick independently and display separate damage numbers; only up to 10 tick numbers of each status are shown. Consequently, each stack uses its own fixed value of 1. For example, separate {{D|Slash}} stacks with seeds of <math>40</math> and <math>80.0195389</math> deal <math>(40 + 1) \times 0.35 = 14.35</math> and <math>(80.0195389 + 1) \times 0.35 = 28.3568382</math>, displayed separately as <math>14</math> and <math>28</math>.

After all applicable multipliers and target defenses are applied, damage pop-ups present the result as a whole number. For non-negative raw damage values, the displayed number is:
:<math>\text{Displayed Damage} = \left\lfloor \text{Raw Damage} + 0.5 \right\rfloor</math>
This is a display-formatting rule only; it does not imply that the underlying raw damage value or the target's health change is rounded to an integer. The fixed value of 1 in the status formula above is part of the raw damage calculation and is unrelated to display rounding.

{{D|Blast}} are not a damage-over-time (DoT) effect but a stack-and-detonate effect, so the per-tick DoT formula above does not apply and there is no DoT "+1" starting value. As with DoT, Blast's intermediate operations use binary32 (f32) arithmetic.

* '''Stacking:''' each Blast proc adds one stack, up to 10 (bosses and eximus-type enemies cap at 4). Each stack lasts 1.5 seconds and records the damage ''H'' of the hit that applied it.
* '''Stack expiry:''' if a stack expires on its own (1.5 s) instead of being consumed by a detonation, it deals a single instance of max(1, 0.3 × ''H'') Blast damage.
* '''Detonation:''' once stacks reach the cap (10; bosses 4), or the enemy dies at any stack count, the currently active stacks are not settled individually but are combined into a single 5-meter radial Blast centered on the enemy, dealing 3 × (sum of the active stacks' ''H''). This radial has no distance falloff within 5 m, and the stacks are cleared afterward. Death detonation likewise uses the fixed ×3 and does not scale with the current stack count.

===Lifetime Damage===
Lifetime damage is a derived damage stat that is based on the total amount of damage that a weapon can deal before it depletes its ammo reserve. [[Melee]] weapons, [[Battery Weapon]]s or rechargable weapons, and [[Exalted Weapon]]s (assuming [[Energy]] is always restored) will deal infinite damage over their in-game use since they are always available and are not reliant on [[Pickups|ammo pickups]] or [[Squad Ammo Restore]]s.
